[title] Result: 2.4x more requests per second
[body] Same hardware: 8 GPUs, same latency target
[body] Median response time unchanged
[body] Measured on a real chat workload

novice.takeaway: Using the same hardware and latency requirements, the new system handled 2.4x more requests per second without slowing down typical response times, tested on real chat data.
questions: How was 'real chat workload' data collected or defined?
Does this improvement generalize to other GPU counts?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to believe their system significantly improves efficiency without sacrificing speed.

peer.takeaway: The described optimizations achieved 2.4x more requests per second on the same hardware without hurting median latency, on a real chat workload.
questions: Is the 2.4x measured at p99 or median latency SLO?
How does 'real chat workload' compare to prior benchmarks?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants viewers to believe their system doubles-plus throughput without sacrificing latency in practice.

expert.takeaway: The combined optimizations achieved a measured 2.4x throughput gain on the same hardware without sacrificing median latency, validated on a real chat workload.
questions: What percentile latency target was used, not just median?
How does p99 latency compare, not just median?
What is the baseline system for comparison?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to accept the 2.4x throughput gain as validated and practically meaningful.
